limits: The previous goal turn made progress at source 9d8b4b8b and canonical commit 9818e595. This turn continues CSP5 and leaves CSP4 done.

The original temporary writers remove operator files in twelve scenarios, with thirteen failed test events including the parent. The test-only hooks expose the existing write, publication, and cleanup boundaries without correcting the unsafe removal.

The ownership failures cover ordinary projection markers, replacement journals, and journaled projection markers. Each path loses changed bytes, identical-byte replacement files, paths recreated after publication, and replacements made after a partial write.
A separate Go overlay restores the original projection-marker reader. It accepts a valid JSON marker padded beyond the 4 MiB limit. The corrected bounded reader refuses it without changing its bytes.

workspaceRecordWriter owns temporary creation, bounded publication, and checked cleanup. It records native identity, access, and the actual written prefix, and keeps the file open until cleanup finishes. Unknown changes remain preserved.

Before publication, the writer rechecks its candidate, its destination snapshot, and cancellation. Journal publication cannot replace an existing destination. Marker publication replaces only the earlier destination state.

Cleanup uses a separate 30-second context after cancellation, checks identity, bytes, and access, and synchronizes its removal. Cleanup errors join the original failure. These records remain in memory.
Additional tests cover access changes, late candidate and destination changes, cancellation, owned partial cleanup, short writes, exact 4 MiB publication, oversize refusal, and journal collisions.

The shared bounded reader serves markers, journals, and endpoint projections with their existing caller-selected limits. It checks regular-file identity and stability and uses native non-following access where available.

All 213 workspace and two CLI command race test events pass without failures or skips. Final ago and prose checks pass. Linux and Windows test binaries compile; native execution and physical power-loss behavior remain unqualified.
The binary stores no new user setting or marker/journal format. Ordinary markers retain their explicit file mode. Journal writes retain their prior umask and inherited access behavior.
